title: The plate of three things
hook: on this plate are three things, truth, contentment and reflection, the seal on the Granth (Mundavani, ang 1429)
tomorrow: The Lord stood to finish the work

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Chaubole: love that even a king couldn't buy. Your line was four voices. In a disagreement, did you let their voice have a turn? Day one thousand two hundred eight.

A steel plate, a thaal, set down on a cloth. In a Sikh home or a gurdwara you might see one holding karah prashad, or food for a guest. Now turn to Ang fourteen hundred twenty-nine, near the very end of the Guru Granth Sahib, and Guru Arjan sets down a plate of his own. He tells you exactly what's on it. Not sweets, not bread. Three things, and then a fourth that holds the others up. It's called the Mundavani, and it comes near the close of the Granth like a seal on a letter.
screen: `A STEEL PLATE ON A CLOTH.` → `ANG 1429.` → `A SEAL ON A LETTER.`

segments.voice: Here it is, paraphrased. On this plate, three things have been placed: truth, contentment, and reflection. The nectar of the Lord's Name has been placed here too, the support of all. Whoever eats it, whoever enjoys it, is saved. This can't be given up; keep it always in your heart. The dark world-ocean is crossed by holding to the Lord's feet; Nanak, all of this is the Lord's own spreading out. Mundavani is often explained as a seal, the kind pressed into wax to close a letter. So near its close, the Guru Granth Sahib names what was inside it all along. Take the three one at a time. Sat, truth: not only telling the truth, but living close to what's real. Santokh, contentment: enough, the end of the endless more. Vichar, reflection: thinking it over, turning the teaching in the mind. Then the Name, amrit naam, laid on the plate beside them as the thing everything rests on. Notice the verbs. Eat. Enjoy. Keep it in your heart. The Guru doesn't describe the plate as something to admire on a shelf. It's a meal. Sikhs read the Mundavani at the completion of a full reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, so a long reading ends at a table. After all those pages, the seal says, this is what you're taking home: truth to stand on, enough to rest in, reflection to grow by, and the Name to feed them.
screen: `THREE THINGS ON THE PLATE.` · `MUNDAVANI: A SEAL.` · `SAT, SANTOKH, VICHAR.` · `EAT IT, KEEP IT IN YOUR HEART.` · then, large: `TRUTH, CONTENTMENT, REFLECTION.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: set out a plate with three things. Any plate, any three small things nearby: a coin, a key, a leaf, a cup. Lay them down one at a time, and give each a name as you do. Truth. Contentment. Reflection. Then sit with the plate in front of you. Ask quietly which of the three your day needs most. Don't solve anything. Just look at the plate, and breathe. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you look. The bell holds the time.
Mundavani. The seal: Guru Arjan's plate of truth, contentment and reflection, with the Lord's Name, near the close of the Guru Granth Sahib. Today's word.
Your line: truth, contentment, reflection. Today, at one meal, before the first bite, name the three to yourself, and let the food remind you of the plate. Day one thousand two hundred eight.
